chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the waiting period (iddah) of a woman in mut'ah (temporary marriage) if the husband who enjoyed her dies? He said: 'Four months and ten days.'

He said, then he said: 'O Zurarah, in all marriages, if the husband dies, the waiting period upon the woman is four months and ten days, whether she is free or a slave, and regardless of whether the marriage was mut'ah, permanent marriage (tazwij), or ownership by right (of a concubine).'

And the waiting period of the divorced woman is three months, and for the slave woman who is divorced, it is half of what is upon the free woman, and similarly, the waiting period of the mut'ah woman upon her is like that of the slave woman.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman in temporary marriage if her husband dies?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via Zurarah, the universality of the four-month-and-ten-day waiting period (Iddah al-Wafā) is emphasized, applying equally to permanent, temporary (Mut'ah), and ownership-based marriages for both free and slave women. This establishes a key jurisprudential principle in Shia fiqh that the death of the husband triggers a uniform waiting period regardless of the marital contract's specific nature, distinguishing it clearly from the three-month period for divorce. The hadith underscores the consistency of divine law across different social statuses, reinforcing the structural integrity of family law in the Imami tradition.
